title: doppler shifted transient sodium detection by keck/hires
abstract: we carried out the first high-resolution transit observations of the exoplanet wasp-49 ab with keck/hires. upon custom wavelength calibration we achieve a doppler rv precision of $<$ 60 ${\rm m\,s}^{-1}$. this is an improvement in rv stability of roughly 240 ${\rm m\,s}^{-1}$ with respect to the instrument standard. we report an average sodium flux residual of $δ\mathcal{f}_{nad}/ \mathcal{f}_{\star} (λ) \sim$ 3.2 $\pm$ 0.4 $\%$ (8.0 $σ$) comparable to previous studies. interestingly, an average doppler shift of -6.2 $\pm$ 0.5 ${\rm km\,s}^{-1}$ (12.4 $σ$) is identified offset from the exoplanet rest frame. the velocity residuals \textit{in time} trace a blueshift (v$_{γ, ingress} \sim$ -10.3 $\pm$ 1.9 ${\rm km\,s}^{-1}$) to redshift (v$_{γ, egress} \sim$ +4.1 $\pm$ 1.5 ${\rm km\,s}^{-1}$) suggesting the origin of the observed sodium is unlikely from the atmosphere of the planet. the average na light curves indicate a depth of $δ\mathcal{f}_{nad} /\mathcal{f}_{\star} (t) \sim$ 0.47 $\pm$ 0.04 % (11.7 $σ$) enduring $\lesssim$ 90 minutes with a half-max duration of $\sim$ 40.1 minutes. frequent high-resolution spectroscopic observations will be able to characterize the periodicity of the observed doppler shifts. considering the origin of the transient sodium gas is of unknown geometry, a co-orbiting natural satellite may be a likely source.
